findings.description: The user_data script contains a hardcoded AWS access key ID and secret access key in plaintext. This data is visible to anyone with access to the instance metadata/console or the Terraform state, resulting in credential leakage and potential account compromise.

The EBS volume does not enable encryption (encrypted is not set to true), so data at rest on the volume is stored in plaintext and vulnerable to exposure if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are shared.
The EBS snapshot is created from an unencrypted volume and does not specify encryption, so the snapshot data is stored unencrypted and could be exposed if shared or accessed by unauthorized parties.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from anywhere on the internet.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0. While this may be intended for a public web server, combined with the lack of encryption/TLS this exposes the service to unauthenticated internet-wide access without any restriction.
The security group allows all outbound traffic (all ports/protocols) to 0.0.0.0/0, which increases attack surface for data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to direct internet access.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to direct internet access.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used for VPC flow logs does not configure server-side encryption or a public access block, and force_destroy is enabled, risking exposure of sensitive network log data and accidental data loss.
